2027-03-11.title: Thursday of the fifth week of the Great Fast
readings: Sarah dies; Abraham, a stranger, asks for a burial place
The hope laid up for you in heaven
No sign but the sign of Jonah
2027-03-11.verse: I am a stranger and an alien residing among you; give me property among you for a burying place, so that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
theo: “Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years… And Sarah died at Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan; and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.” The man who did not weep on Mount Moriah weeps now beside his wife. Scripture does not hide his tears; faith does not forbid grief, it gives grief a direction. Then Abraham “rose up from beside his dead” and spoke to the Hittites: “I am a stranger and an alien residing among you; give me property among you for a burying place.” After more than sixty years in the land God had promised him, Abraham does not own a single field. The promise is real, but it is still ahead. The Hittites answer him with honour, “you are a mighty prince among us,” and Abraham bows before “the people of the land.” The father of believers deals courteously and justly with people of another nation and another faith, a lesson our multi-religious land knows well. The Letter to the Hebrews explains his patience: the patriarchs “died in faith without having received the promises… They confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth.” An early Christian writer, the author of the Letter to Diognetus, said the same of Christians: they live in their own countries, but as sojourners; every foreign land is a homeland to them, and every homeland a foreign land (in substance).

St Paul tells the Colossians where the Christian homeland is: “we always thank God… for we have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love that you have for all the saints, because of the hope laid up for you in heaven.” Faith, love and hope: hope is the treasure stored up ahead, and it gives strength to faith and love today. That is why we can grieve without despair, as Paul says elsewhere, “so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.” Our Church prays for the departed at every Holy Qurbono, and in the Great Fast we remember them with special love. In the Gospel the Pharisees and Sadducees ask Jesus for “a sign from heaven.” He answers that they can read the sky, red at evening, red in the morning, “but you cannot interpret the signs of the times.” And he gives them only one sign: “An evil and adulterous generation asks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.” Jonah came out of the sea monster after three days; Jesus will come out of the tomb on the third day. The Resurrection is the sign that answers Abraham's grave, Sarah's death and every Christian funeral. In three weeks we will sing it at Easter.
outline: Ask: where is my true home?
Point 2 · A stranger and an alien
Living in the land of promise without owning it.
Hope laid up in heaven, proved by the empty tomb.
“I am a stranger and an alien residing among you.”
live: Visit a cemetery or pray at home this week for a departed member of your family, and have a Holy Qurbono offered for them if you can.
Read the signs of the times (Matthew 16:3)
Spend ten minutes this week asking what God is saying to you through the events around you, and write one line about it.
2027-03-11.prayer: Lord God, Abraham wept for Sarah and lived as a stranger in the land you promised him, trusting in a better country. Comfort all who mourn, give eternal rest to our departed, and keep our eyes on the hope laid up for us in heaven. Give us the one sign that is enough, the sign of Jonah, your Son risen from the tomb. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono the Church remembers her departed and offers the sacrifice of the One who came out of the tomb on the third day.

quick: Sarah died at Hebron; Abraham mourned and wept for her and, as a stranger, asked the Hittites for a burial place.
Paul thanks God for the Colossians' faith and love, born of the hope laid up for them in heaven.
Jesus refused to give a sign from heaven except the sign of Jonah.
2027-03-11.action: Pray for a departed member of your family by name.
2027-03-11.question: Do I live as a citizen of heaven or as if this world were my only home?

family.explain: When Sarah died, Abraham cried for her. He loved her very much. Even though God had promised him the land, Abraham did not yet own any of it, and he had to ask for a place to bury her. Abraham knew that his real home was with God. Jesus rose from the tomb on the third day, so we know that death is not the end.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom shall we remember in our prayers tonight?”

illus: A Malayali nurse who had worked in the Gulf for twenty-eight years came home for her mother's funeral in Mavelikara. Her colleagues abroad had always called her the one from Kerala; in her own village the neighbours now called her the one from the Gulf. Standing by the grave after the prayers, she said to the priest that she did not belong anywhere any more. The old priest pointed to the cross on the tomb and said: neither did Abraham. That is why God gave him a city. She has kept the funeral card with that line written on the back.

pm.open: Lord, our true home is with you. Keep our hearts fixed on the hope you have prepared for us. Amen.
share: Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her (Genesis 23:2). Have I allowed myself to grieve with faith?
I am a stranger and an alien residing among you (Genesis 23:4). Where am I too attached to this world?
No sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah (Matthew 16:4). What signs do I demand from God?
interc: For all who are mourning a husband, wife or parent.
For our departed relatives, friends and benefactors.
For migrants and those who live far from home.
For good relations between people of different faiths in our land.
For those who seek signs, that they may find the risen Christ.
pm.close: Father, you call us to be pilgrims on the earth and citizens of heaven. Comfort the grieving, receive our departed into your light, and let the sign of your Son's Resurrection keep our hope alive. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today Sarah dies, and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her (Genesis 23:2). The great man of faith is not ashamed to weep. Faith does not take away our tears; it gives them hope.

Abraham says to the Hittites: I am a stranger and an alien residing among you; give me property among you for a burying place (Genesis 23:4). He has lived for decades in the promised land, and he does not own even a grave. The patriarchs confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth (Hebrews 11:13).
Paul thanks God for the Colossians' faith and love because of the hope laid up for you in heaven (Colossians 1:5). Hope is the treasure ahead that strengthens us today.

When the Pharisees and Sadducees ask for a sign, Jesus says: no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah (Matthew 16:4). Jonah came out after three days; Christ rose on the third day. Let us pray today for our departed and walk toward Easter as pilgrims full of hope. Amen.
kids: Children, when Sarah died, Abraham cried, because he loved her. It is all right to be sad when someone we love dies. But Jesus rose from the dead on the third day, so we have hope that we will see our loved ones again with God. Tonight, pray for someone in your family who has gone to God.

intro: Theme: “I am a stranger and an alien residing among you.”
Abraham's tears for Sarah, his life as a pilgrim in the land of promise, and the sign of Jonah that answers every grave.

q: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
But we do not want you to be uninformed, brothers and sisters, about those who have died, so that you may not grieve as others do who have no hope.
points.apply: Pray this week by name for your departed relatives and friends.

sub: Courtesy toward the people of the land.
q: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and give ear to my cry; do not hold your peace at my tears. For I am your passing guest, an alien, like all my forebears.
All of these died in faith without having received the promises, but from a distance they saw and greeted them. They confessed that they were strangers and foreigners on the earth,
points.apply: Let go of one thing this week that ties your heart too tightly to this world.

sub: Reading the sky, missing the times.
q: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Prepare one concrete way to celebrate the Resurrection with your family at Easter.

concl: Abraham owned nothing in the land but a grave, yet he died rich in hope.
The risen Christ is the sign that answers every death and every tear.
2027-03-11.resolve: Live the rest of the Fast as a pilgrim, praying daily for the departed.
